title: Evidence causal timeline
description: Objective: implement evidence, artifact, rejection, session-coordination, and causal timeline inspection with cursor provenance. Deliverable: evidence/timeline modules. NOT in scope: altering or upgrading evidence. Hard dependencies: Generated control-room client and Session coordination fabric. Owned paths: apps/control-room/src/evidence/** and apps/control-room/src/timeline/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test.
definitionOfDone: Every rendered fact links to provenance, cursor, actor/session/effect, and exact digest where applicable.
Rejected commands, cursor gaps, recovery markers, and typed session messages remain visible without becoming authority.
Large timelines paginate and resume without silent gaps.
taskRails: The standalone control room displays daemon truth and nextAllowedCommands; it never derives authority, readiness, or evidence strength.
Every fact is text/icon/color encoded, keyboard accessible, provenance-drillable, and honest under degraded data.
IDE adapters remain thin optional launch/discover/embed shells with no product logic. Keep modules below 400 lines; explicit owned paths only.

implementationPlan.description: timeline-contract.ts — presentation vocabulary, no authority, no I/O. Declare: TIMELINE_ROW_KINDS as a frozen array (EVENT, REJECTED, RESTART_GAP) with its derived union; the row record types carrying the spec-3.2 provenance fields (eventSequence, eventId, actor, sessionId, effectId, leaseEpoch, timestamp, typedLink) with every one of them nullable rather than optional, since exactOptionalPropertyTypes is ON and an absent field must be representable as ABSENT rather than missing; a frozen TIMELINE_REFUSAL_CODES vocabulary with refusal LAYERS (INPUT, PAGING, RENDER) following the layered-refusal precedent, because more than one layer can refuse and the epic rail requires tests to pin which; and the cursor-state record (appliedSequence, latestSequence, live). CRITICAL IMPORT BAN: CURSOR_GAP is defined in packages/store/src/subscriptions/subscription-contracts.ts and packages/coordination/src/coordination-contracts.ts, and this app may import NEITHER — its dependency set is @moe/contracts, @moe/control-room-client and @moe/control-room-model. The gap outcome arrives as payload data through the gated client, so pin the string literal locally and treat it as data. Reuse FieldProvenance and UNSTATED from ../data/data-contract.js; do not declare a second provenance vocabulary.

Import ban honoured: the only import is `import type { FieldProvenance } from "../data/data-contract.js"`. Nothing from @moe/store or @moe/coordination — and those are not even declared dependencies of apps/control-room, so the ban is a resolution fact as well as a policy.

Four decisions a reviewer will ask about:

1. TRUNCATION IS NOT A REFUSAL. The plan groups MAX_VIEW_RECORDS with the refusal codes; I gave it a separate TIMELINE_TRUNCATION_CODE instead. Withholding rows already walked would lose truth, so hitting the bound reports `truncation: {code, droppedFromSequence, limit}` on a WALKED result. Separate code means a bounded walk can never be read as a complete one.

2. FOUR CODES, ALL REACHABLE, ONE PER LAYER MINIMUM. TIMELINE_LIMIT_INVALID (INPUT), TIMELINE_SEQUENCE_OUT_OF_ORDER + TIMELINE_CURSOR_NOT_ADVANCING (PAGING), TIMELINE_ROW_KIND_UNSUPPORTED (RENDER). Every layer has a real emitter, so the layer assertion is not decorative. Followed task-f837ce45's rule that an unreachable stable code gets removed rather than kept.

3. TIMELINE_CURSOR_NOT_ADVANCING is an addition beyond the plan's five named cases. A source that says hasMore while handing back a cursor that does not advance would spin the walk forever. Refusing with a stated code is the fail-closed answer; step 3 pins it.

4. NO SEPARATE provenance.eventSequence. The row's `sequence` IS the daemon-stated source event sequence (it is also the `cr.timeline.row.{eventSeq}` identity), so there is exactly one field for it rather than two that can disagree. `leaseEpoch: null` keeps spec 3.2's own meaning — "if leased mutation" — so its absence is a stated fact, not an unknown; every other absence is ABSENT/UNKNOWN.

implementationPlan.description: RED — paging and resume tests, before timeline-page.ts exists. THIS IS DoD 3 AND IT HAS A KNOWN TRAP. The timeline ships filters (cr.timeline.filter.{node|actor|type}), so pages WILL be filtered after fetch — which means the fetched page's hasMore and nextCursor no longer describe the walk. Continuing from them produces an early, successful-looking termination, i.e. exactly the silent gap DoD 3 forbids (mem:gotcha-clamped-page-must-not-trust-unclamped-hasmore, where this shape shipped undetected in the store's rebuild loop). Tests, each asserting code AND layer where it refuses: (a) a page whose rows are partly filtered out must continue from what was KEPT, not from the source's nextCursor — construct a page where the two differ and assert the resulting continuation, since a case where they coincide proves nothing; (b) resuming from a persisted cursor yields the same total row sequence as an uninterrupted walk over the same fixture — compare full sequences, not counts; (c) a CURSOR_GAP outcome surfaces a RESTART_GAP row and does NOT silently resync; (d) MAX_VIEW_RECORDS is enforced and the truncation is reported, never silent; (e) a page arriving out of sequence order refuses rather than being sorted into place, since reordering would be deriving an ordering the daemon did not state.

13 tests written across 6 describes. Every refusal case asserts code AND layer with separate toBe calls (never an or-ed assertion — mem:gotcha-or-ed-layer-assertion-pins-neither-layer).

THE FIXTURES DELIBERATELY DIFFER FROM THE ENVELOPE. `lyingSource` reports nextCursor = lastServed.sequence + 1, so an implementation that continues from the envelope skips exactly one real row per page; `honestSource` reports lastServed.sequence. Test 1 walks 6 rows in pages of 3 through the lying source and asserts [1,2,3,4,5,6] — under an envelope-trusting walk row 4 vanishes silently.

DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN'S LITERAL DoD-3 RULE, and it is load-bearing. The plan transposes the store's fix as `!page.hasMore && kept.length === page.items.length`. Copying that verbatim here does NOT work and would hang the walk: in the store the clamp drops rows the walk NEEDED, but here the display filter drops rows the operator does not want to SEE, and a page emptied by the filter would then never satisfy `kept.length === items.length`, so the loop could never terminate. The correct transposition separates the two droppers:
  - EXAMINED = rows of the page the walk looked at. The filter does not reduce it.
  - ADMITTED = rows that reached the view. The MAX_VIEW_RECORDS bound reduces it.
  - complete = !hasMore && examined === page.rows.length && truncation === null.
That IS the store's condition, with `examined` in place of `kept`. Three tests pin the distinction: the lying-envelope test, "continues past rows the filter removed instead of re-reading them" (page 2 fully filtered out, asserts [1,2,3,7,8,9] and termination), and "reports the walk complete only when the source is exhausted" (final page emptied by the filter still completes, nextCursor 6).

The continuation cursor is the last EXAMINED row's sequence, except when the bound cut a page short, where it is the last ADMITTED row's sequence. Both are recomputed from the walk; page.nextCursor is never read at all, which is what makes step 10's mutation (a) killable.

RESTART GAP: the row is admitted like any other and the walk continues from its own sequence. "Does not silently resync" is pinned by a source spy asserting the served cursors are exactly [null, 3] — a resync from the gap's lastGoodSequence (1) would re-serve and duplicate rows 2-3. The gap's statedCause and gapOutcome are asserted verbatim.

TRUNCATION: proved against MAX_VIEW_RECORDS itself with a generated corpus of MAX_VIEW_RECORDS + 5 rows, and the generated length is asserted first so a sweep that produced nothing cannot pass (mem:pattern-guard-the-case-list-not-just-the-cases). Truncation is deep-equal-asserted as {code: TIMELINE_VIEW_LIMIT_REACHED, droppedFromSequence, limit}, and complete is false.

RESUME: full sequence comparison, not counts — walk-to-bound then resume, concatenated, deep-equal against the uninterrupted walk over the same fixture.

TIMELINE_LIMIT_INVALID is asserted over [0, -1, 1.5, NaN] with a source that THROWS if read, so the test also pins that the bound is checked before any page is fetched.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN — timeline-page.ts. A pure cursor walk over caller-supplied pages: apply the row filter, then recompute the continuation cursor from the rows actually kept, never from the incoming page envelope. Only report the walk complete when the source says there is no more AND nothing was dropped from the final page — the store's fix for this exact bug is `if (!page.hasMore && kept.length === page.items.length) break;` and the same reasoning applies here. Surface CURSOR_GAP as a RESTART_GAP row carrying whatever the daemon stated about the gap; never paper over it and never re-derive the missing span. Enforce MAX_VIEW_RECORDS with an explicit reported truncation. No fetch, no socket, no timer: pages arrive as arguments, so the whole module is deterministic and testable. Keep under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` -> exit 0, "Test Files 14 passed (14) / Tests 189 passed". Suites 13 -> 14, tests 175 -> 189 (+14). `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` -> exit 0. timeline-page.ts is 173 lines, under the 250 rail.

walkTimeline({filter, maxRows, source, startCursor}) -> TimelineWalkResult. Pure: the source is a caller-supplied (cursor) => TimelineSourcePage function, so there is no fetch, socket, timer, or clock anywhere in the module.

page.nextCursor IS NEVER READ. Not in walkTimeline, not in any helper. The continuation is:
  - last EXAMINED row's sequence when the whole page was consumed (the filter having removed rows does not change this);
  - last ADMITTED row's sequence when the view bound cut the page short.
complete = source exhausted AND whole final page examined AND nothing overflowed. See step 3's note for why `admitted` in place of `examined` would hang the walk.

ONE ADDITION BEYOND THE PLAN, and it is a DoD-2 fix rather than scope creep: survivesFilter() exempts RESTART_GAP rows from every filter. A gap belongs to the STREAM, not to a node, actor, or event type, so a node filter would otherwise drop the only visible evidence that the stream is discontinuous — a silent gap arriving through the filter layer instead of the cursor layer. Pinned by a new test ("keeps the gap row visible even when the filter excludes everything else", filter: () => false, asserts the surviving row is the RESTART_GAP). REJECTED rows are deliberately NOT exempt: a rejected command has a real actor and node, so narrowing by actor legitimately narrows it, and DoD 2's "remain visible" is about not hiding it behind a toast.

Termination is a proved property, not an assumption. orderRefusal compares each page's first row against the cursor it was served for, so a source that re-serves a page it already served is refused with TIMELINE_SEQUENCE_OUT_OF_ORDER/PAGING rather than looped over. Combined with the empty-page TIMELINE_CURSOR_NOT_ADVANCING/PAGING guard, every non-advancing source is refused rather than spun.

Gap handling: the RESTART_GAP row is admitted like any other row and the walk continues from the gap row's OWN sequence. lastGoodSequence is never read as a cursor; the spy test asserts the served cursors are exactly [null, 3].

MAX_VIEW_RECORDS and the caller's maxRows are both enforced via limit = Math.min(maxRows, MAX_VIEW_RECORDS); overflow returns the first row that did not fit, so droppedFromSequence names a real row rather than a count. Result rows are frozen.

FOUR HONESTY PROPERTIES BEYOND THE PLAN'S LIST, each because the alternative is a silent lie:
1. A REFUSED walk renders cr.timeline.refusal naming the code AND the layer. Without this a refusal renders as an empty list, which reads as "no events" — the worst possible failure for a forensic surface.
2. TIMELINE_ROW_KIND_UNSUPPORTED/RENDER is exercised by casting a row to an alien kind, so the RENDER layer of the step-2 vocabulary has a real emitter and the row is still rendered rather than dropped.
3. Truncation renders cr.timeline.truncation carrying the code and the sequence it stopped before, so the list cannot just end.
4. A row whose eventId is ABSENT gets NO cr.timeline.jump link (asserted by count), following node-evidence.tsx's EvidenceLink precedent: a link to an unresolvable target presents unreachable evidence as reachable.

DoD 2 filter test: "cannot hide a restart gap behind a node filter" drives the select to a node the gap does not belong to and asserts the gap row survives. This is the surface-level pin of step 4's survivesFilter exemption.

ACCESSIBILITY (task rail 3): kinds are asserted as TEXT ("EVENT", "REJECTED", "RESTART GAP") via cr.timeline.kind.*, so no state is colour- or glyph-only; every row asserts tabindex="0"; the chip/fact counts are asserted EQUAL to the row count (3/3/3) so the §12 "every cr.fact.* has a cr.chip.* descendant" audit keeps counting exactly; PROVENANCE_SHORTCUT_KEY opens the row drill-down from a focused chip, and a negative test asserts it does NOT fire from the row itself, mirroring FactWithProvenance's own target guard.

CONTRACT AMENDMENT NEEDED IN STEP 6: the tests use a daemon-stated `eventType: string | null` on the row base, because §4.5's `type[all▾]` filter axis needs a real field to narrow on. Filtering `type` on row.kind instead would have made the type filter able to hide REJECTED rows. timeline-contract.ts gains that one nullable field in step 6.

DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN'S NAMED REUSE, deliberate. The plan says reuse FactWithProvenance from shell/provenance-panel.js. Two concrete lies it would have forced:
  - FixtureProvenance renders leaseEpoch === null as "not a leased mutation". The daemon omits that field both when the mutation was not leased and when it stated nothing, and this surface cannot tell those apart, so it renders UNKNOWN and says so in a comment.

Truth presentation is still not reimplemented: the row's claim goes FactRow -> Fact -> TruthChip -> describeTruthClass, so the chip remains a structural child. The provenance drill-down is a per-row <details> instead of the shell popover, which is strictly more visible than a popover.

EVERY §2.9 FIELD HAS ITS OWN TESTID AND AN EXACT-VALUE ASSERTION (toBe, not toContain): argv (as an ordered list of cr.evidence.argv.{i} items, so quoting is never flattened into one string), cwd, env fingerprint, started, ended, exit, output digest, output tail, base SHA, head SHA, dirty-tree digest, plus per-artifact digests under cr.evidence.artifact.{artifactId}.

DIGESTS IN FULL, pinned twice over. Each digest is asserted equal to the full 71-char literal, and a whole-container sweep asserts the rendered text contains neither "…" nor "...". The second assertion is the one that survives refactors: it catches an ellipsis introduced anywhere on the surface, including in a field a later task adds.

NON-ZERO EXIT: exitCode 2 renders as exactly "2", and the container text is swept for four softening phrases ("passed with warnings", "mostly", "partial success", "non-blocking"). Matches evidence-j1.tsx's existing contract that a failed run is displayed as itself.

ABSENT stays UNKNOWN and is machine-readable: every absent cell asserts BOTH textContent === UNSTATED AND data-provenance === "ABSENT", and a sibling field in the same render asserts "DAEMON_STATED", so the test cannot pass by rendering everything as absent.

NO MUTATION AFFORDANCE, asserted structurally rather than by absence of a string: zero elements with a cr.action.* testid, and every <button> in the tree must match /^cr\.chip\./ — so the only button a read-only surface may hold is the structural truth chip. A rerun button would fail on both counts.

SESSION MESSAGES: rendered through the existing AdvisoryMessage/AdvisoryReceipt pair from data-contract.js, with advisoryOnly and authority asserted as the literals "advisory only" and "NONE". Those two literals are the whole mechanism keeping a typed session message visible without authority, so they are asserted directly rather than inferred from the message rendering at all.

TWO ADDITIONS BEYOND THE PLAN'S LIST:
1. cr.evidence.compare is §2.9's third pinned component. It renders ONLY a daemon-supplied comparison record {againstReceiptId, statedOutcome}; with none supplied it says "No comparison supplied." Both arms are asserted. Nothing is computed — the UI never compares two digests itself, which would be deriving evidence strength. cr.action.evidence-rerun stays unrendered as out of scope.

comments.content:
POST-REVIEW REGRESSION IN AN OWNED FILE — found and fixed after complete_task. QA read this before diffing.

After I handed off, an external edit changed ONE line in apps/control-room/src/timeline/timeline-page.ts:

  const lastExamined = page.rows.at(-1);   ->   const lastExamined = shown.at(-1);

`shown` is the FILTERED array; `page.rows` is the EXAMINED array. This is exactly the conflation the module header warns against, and it is not cosmetic — it HANGS.

Failure mechanism: when a filter removes a page's trailing rows the cursor under-advances; when a filter empties a page entirely `shown.at(-1)` is undefined, so the cursor does not move at all, the source re-serves the same page, and the walk spins forever.

Measured, not reasoned: `npx vitest run src/timeline/timeline-page.test.ts` ran 119.34s with "tests 0ms" and died with "Worker exited unexpectedly" — the fork was killed before a single test executed. Note this is why suite counts matter (mem:gotcha-mutation-drill-blind-to-broken-syntax): a hung worker reports zero tests, so watching only the test number shows nothing failing.

FIXED by restoring `page.rows.at(-1)` and adding a comment at the line naming the symptom, so the next person to try the same substitution sees why it is wrong before running it.

Re-verified after the fix:
- my four suites alone: 4 files / 55 tests, exit 0
- tsc errors inside apps/control-room/src/timeline and src/evidence: zero
- full package: 275 tests pass; the one red FILE is FOREIGN — src/doctor/doctor-console.test.tsx, another agent's red-first TDD whose ./doctor-console.js does not exist yet. Not my path, not my defect. Same shared-tree pattern as the board-surface red I waited out before handing off.

The verification evidence in my complete_task (19 files / 268 tests, exit 0) was accurate when recorded at 12:51. It is no longer reproducible at this instant, solely because of the foreign doctor-console file. Re-run the package gate once that worker lands their GREEN, or verify my work in isolation with the two commands above.

planningNotes.risks:
THE ONE THAT WILL BITE — DoD 3. This timeline has filters, so pages are filtered after fetch, which means the fetched page's hasMore and nextCursor stop describing the walk. Continuing from them terminates early and reports success, which is a silent gap: strictly worse than a crash, and precisely what DoD 3 forbids. This exact shape shipped undetected in packages/store/src/projections/projection-rebuild.ts and was caught only by a mutation-drill survivor (mem:gotcha-clamped-page-must-not-trust-unclamped-hasmore). A TEST THAT PROVES NOTHING — the paging tests must construct a page where the kept rows and the source envelope genuinely DIFFER. Every store test that missed this bug used a page where they coincided; the bug needs a page straddling the boundary, which existed in no fixture.

Under jsdom the global URL resolves a relative specifier against the document base, so new URL('.', base) yields http://localhost:3000/... and fileURLToPath then throws 'The URL must be of scheme file'. Already documented in data-ban.test.ts's header — read it before writing the scan.

THE AUTHORITY LINE — 'causal timeline' means rendering causal links the daemon STATED (aggregate, command ID, effect, lease epoch). It never means inferring causality from ordering, and no surface here may sort or rank by truth class. Task rail 2 is explicit that this app never derives authority, readiness, or evidence strength.

HONESTY DETAILS — digests render in full, because a truncated digest cannot be compared and an incomparable fact is not evidence. A non-zero exit renders as itself, matching evidence-j1.tsx. An ABSENT field renders UNKNOWN and never borrows a neighbouring row's value.
